## 12. `callisto-vcs`

**Purpose.** One `GitDataSource` trait, two backends, and a selector that picks between them
per operation so every other crate that needs Git — `callisto-graph` (tags, changed-since,
publish SHAs) and `callisto-conventional` (commit-severity inference windows) — calls one API
regardless of whether native `gix` is available on the running target.

**License:** MIT/Apache-2.0 (§16 — despite sitting below AGPL `callisto-graph` in the
dependency graph, this crate depends on nothing but `callisto-model`, so nothing AGPL leaks
into it; the permissive/AGPL boundary is a one-way constraint on what a permissive crate may
depend on, not on who may depend on a permissive crate).
**Milestone:** v0.1 (§17 — repository discovery and tag/commit reads are load-bearing for
`status`'s `last_tag_for`/`changed_since_last_tag` from the first shipped milestone).

### V.0 Dependencies and boundaries

| Edge | Kind | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `callisto-vcs → callisto-model` | normal | `ApplyPermit`, `CommandError`, `CommandRunner`, `CommitRecord`, `CommitSha`, `CommitWalkError`, `CommitWalker`, `TagName` |
| `gix` | normal, `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))` only | native backend (§V.4) |
| `globset` | normal | tag-glob matching, shared identically by both backends (§V.4, §V.5) |
| `dunce` | normal | UNC-prefix-stripped canonicalization before `gix::discover` (§20) |
| `callisto-fixtures` | **dev** | none today — grep confirms zero `callisto_fixtures::` usage in this crate's tests (§15 precedent); listed for completeness only if a future fixture corpus is added |

**Deliberately absent:** `callisto-graph`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-format`. This crate
has no concept of a `Package`, a manifest, or a changeset — it answers exactly two kinds of
question, "what does history/refs say" and "write this ref," using only `CommitSha`/`TagName`
as vocabulary. `callisto-moon` never depends on this crate at all (not even for the shell
backend): gix's mmap-based object reads hit `ENOSYS` under `wasm32-wasip1` (verified by spike,
§Track 0), so `GitRepository::discover` is `cfg`-gated out entirely on that target and would
contribute nothing `callisto-moon` could use — the WASM extension's own exec seam calls
`CommandRunner` directly against moon's `exec_command` host function instead, without going
through this crate's `ShellGit` wrapper.

**What this crate is not responsible for:** deciding *which* ref format a tag name should take
(`tag_template` resolution is `callisto-model`'s `last_tag_for`, §M.9.4, plus
`callisto-graph`'s `git tag --list` glob execution, §G.9.1 — this crate only ever receives an
already-resolved literal name or glob string), and deciding *when* a tag should be created
(§9.1's "never at `version` time" rule is enforced by callers; `create_tag` will happily create
a tag the instant it's called).

### V.1 Module layout

```
callisto-vcs/
├── Cargo.toml   # deps: callisto-model, thiserror, miette, globset, dunce; gix (non-wasm32
│                  target only). dev-deps: callisto-model (test-util), tempfile.
└── src/
    ├── lib.rs     # VcsError, GitCommit alias, GitVcsProvider, GitDataSource, GitRepository,
    │                CommitWalker bridge (§V.7)
    ├── access.rs  # GitAccess — per-operation native/shell selection (§V.6)
    └── shell.rs   # ShellGit — CommandRunner-shelled backend (§V.5)
```

### V.2 Errors — `VcsError` (`lib.rs`)

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, thiserror::Error, miette::Diagnostic, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum VcsError {
    #[error("failed to discover Git repository at `{path}`: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E050), help("Ensure target directory is inside a valid Git repository."))]
    RepoNotFound { path: PathBuf, message: String },

    #[error("git error: {0}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E051))]
    Git(String),

    #[error("reference `{ref_name}` was not found")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E052), help("Check if reference or tag exists in local or remote Git refs."))]
    RefNotFound { ref_name: String },

    #[error("tag glob pattern `{pattern}` is not a valid glob: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E053), help("Fix the glob syntax or use a literal tag name."))]
    InvalidGlob { pattern: String, message: String },

    /// Wraps a `CommandError` surfaced by the shell backend — e.g. `git` itself couldn't be
    /// spawned. Kept `transparent` so callers that only care about the underlying
    /// `CommandError` can match through it regardless of which backend served the call.
    #[error(transparent)]
    Command(#[from] CommandError),
}
```

`callisto-graph` wraps this transparently (`GraphError::Vcs`, §error-taxonomy — no dedicated
E-code of its own; the four codes above are `VcsError`'s own and survive unchanged through the
transparent wrap). `E050`–`E053` is this crate's own contiguous block, chosen not to collide
with `callisto-model`'s or `callisto-graph`'s ranges (§error-taxonomy).

**`RefNotFound` is not always an error at the trait level.** `GitDataSource::resolve_commit`
returns `Ok(None)` for an unresolvable ref — a caller-visible "no bound" signal, not a failure.
`VcsError::RefNotFound` exists for the one place resolution failure *is* fatal:
`GitDataSource::commits_since`'s `since_ref: Some(r)` where `r` fails to resolve (§V.4) — the
distinction matters because a caller that explicitly bounded its walk must never silently fall
back to unbounded history (§V.4's regression note).

### V.3 `GitDataSource` — the unified access trait (`lib.rs`)

```rust
pub type GitCommit = callisto_model::CommitRecord;

pub trait GitDataSource {
    fn head_sha(&self) -> Result<CommitSha, VcsError>;
    fn list_tags(&self, glob: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<TagName>, VcsError>;
    fn resolve_commit(&self, refname: &str) -> Result<Option<CommitSha>, VcsError>;
    fn commits_since(&self, since_ref: Option<&str>, pathspecs: &[PathBuf])
        -> Result<Vec<GitCommit>, VcsError>;
    fn create_tag(&self, name: &str, target_sha: &CommitSha, message: Option<&str>,
        permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), VcsError>;
    fn create_floating_major(&self, major_name: &str, target_sha: &CommitSha,
        permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), VcsError>;
}
```

`GitCommit` is a type alias for `callisto_model::CommitRecord`, not a redeclaration — a commit
crosses the `CommitWalker` seam (§V.7, Layer 1) without a conversion, and there is exactly one
definition of "what a commit looks like" in the workspace. Three implementors: `GitRepository`
(§V.4), `ShellGit` (§V.5), and `GitAccess` (§V.6, the one callers actually construct).
`create_tag`/`create_floating_major` take an `ApplyPermit` (§M.10) because they write a ref; a
dry run mints no permit and so cannot reach either call.

`list_tags`'s `glob` parameter is matched with `globset::Glob` — **identically** by both
backends (§V.4 filters `gix`'s own reference iterator locally; §V.5 always fetches the
*unfiltered* `git tag --list` and filters locally too, deliberately never delegating to `git
tag --list <pattern>`'s own, different glob dialect) — so tag selection is byte-identical
regardless of which backend served the request. A pattern that fails to compile is
`Err(VcsError::InvalidGlob)`, never a silent "match everything," since a malformed
`tag_template`-derived glob silently matching every tag in the repo would let `last_tag_for`
(§M.9.4) pick an unrelated package's tag.

### V.4 `GitRepository` — native `gix` backend (`lib.rs`)

```rust
pub struct GitRepository { /* wraps gix::Repository, cfg(not(wasm32)) only */ }

impl GitRepository {
    pub fn discover(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self, VcsError>;
    pub fn head_sha(&self) -> Result<CommitSha, VcsError>;
    pub fn list_tags(&self, glob_pattern: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<TagName>, VcsError>;
    pub fn resolve_commit(&self, refname: &str) -> Result<Option<CommitSha>, VcsError>;
    pub fn commits_since_with_pathspec(&self, since: Option<&CommitSha>, pathspecs: &[PathBuf])
        -> Result<Vec<GitCommit>, VcsError>;
    pub fn create_tag(&self, name: &str, target_sha: &CommitSha, message: Option<&str>,
        permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), VcsError>;
    pub fn create_floating_major(&self, major_name: &str, target_sha: &CommitSha,
        permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), VcsError>;
}
```

`discover` runs `path` through `dunce::canonicalize` first (falling back to the raw path if
canonicalization itself fails) before handing it to `gix::discover` — the same UNC-stripping
concern as every other canonicalization site in the workspace (§20). Every method is `cfg`-split
in its body: the non-`wasm32` half does the real `gix` call; the `wasm32` half is either an
always-`Err` (`discover`, `create_tag`, `create_floating_major` — no meaningful degraded
behavior for a write or for the root discovery call itself) or a harmless always-empty/`Ok(None)`
(`list_tags`, `resolve_commit` — a caller on that target never actually reaches these, since
`discover` already failed upstream, but the bodies stay total rather than panicking).

**`resolve_commit` treats an unresolvable ref as `Ok(None)`, not `Err`** — chained `let...else`
steps (rev-parse → object → peel-to-commit) each degrade to `None` on failure. This is a
deliberate two-tier contract with `commits_since`: an *implicit* absence of a bound
(`since_ref: None`) and an *explicit* bound that fails to resolve are different situations, and
only `GitDataSource::commits_since` (not `resolve_commit` itself) is where the second case
becomes `Err(VcsError::RefNotFound)`.

**Regression fixed by this shape: no silent unbounded fallback.** An earlier version of this
method resolved `since_ref` *internally* and, on a resolution failure, fell through to walking
the entire history unbounded — a correctness bug (already-released commits could re-surface
into changelog/severity inference) masquerading as graceful degradation. The fix routes
`since_ref` resolution through `resolve_commit` and an explicit `Ok(None) =>
Err(RefNotFound)` step in `commits_since`, so an unresolvable *explicit* bound is always
surfaced as an error; `since_ref: None` (no bound requested at all) is unaffected.

`commits_since_with_pathspec` walks `gix::Repository::rev_walk` from `HEAD`, excluding every
SHA reachable from `since` (computed as its own full walk, collected into a `HashSet`, so
membership is checked with `continue` rather than terminating the outer walk with `break` — a
topological walk can visit `since` before it has emitted every commit on a branch that
diverged *before* `since`, and a `break` would silently drop those still-queued commits; this
was a real bug, pinned by `test_commits_since_with_pathspec_includes_pre_tag_branch_commits`).
Merge commits (more than one parent) are always skipped, matching `git log --no-merges`.
Path-scoping diffs each commit's tree against its first parent (or the empty tree, for a root
commit) with `track_rewrites(None)` — a rename is reported as a separate `Deletion`+`Addition`
rather than one `Rewrite`, and either half matching a pathspec counts as "touched," which is
also why a file moved *out of* a matching directory still shows that commit as touching it.
Commit message CRLF sequences are normalized to `\n` in both `summary` and `body`.

### V.5 `ShellGit` — `CommandRunner`-shelled backend (`shell.rs`)

```rust
pub struct ShellGit<'r> { /* runner: &'r dyn CommandRunner, root: PathBuf */ }

impl<'r> ShellGit<'r> {
    pub fn new(runner: &'r dyn CommandRunner, root: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self;
}
```

Implements `GitDataSource` by shelling exactly the `git` subcommands each operation needs,
consolidating five previously independent hand-rolled fallbacks (`callisto-graph`'s
`changed.rs`, `tags.rs`, `commands/tag.rs`, `aggregate.rs`, and `callisto-conventional`'s
`window.rs`). Works on every target, including `wasm32`, since it never touches `gix`.

| Operation | Shell command |
|---|---|
| `head_sha` | `git rev-parse HEAD` |
| `list_tags` | `git tag --list`, filtered locally with `globset` (§V.3) |
| `resolve_commit` | `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <ref>^{commit}` — non-zero or empty stdout is `Ok(None)`, never `Err` |
| `commits_since` | `git log --no-merges --format=<RS>%H<US>%B <since>..HEAD\|HEAD [-- <pathspecs>]` |
| `create_tag` | `git tag [-a -m <message>] -- <name> <sha>` |
| `create_floating_major` | `git tag -f -- <major_name> <sha>` |

`commits_since` deliberately does **not** pre-resolve `since_ref` with a separate `rev-parse`
round-trip: an unresolvable `since_ref` already makes `git log <since_ref>..HEAD` itself exit
non-zero, which the method surfaces as `Err(VcsError::Git(..))` exactly like any other `git
log` failure — one shell call either way, and the same no-silent-unbounded-walk guarantee
§V.4 documents for the native backend, achieved by a different mechanism (a failing command
instead of a resolved-then-checked ref).

`--format=` uses two control characters as delimiters, never present in ordinary commit text:
`\u{1e}` (record separator) immediately before each commit's SHA, and `\u{1f}` (field
separator) between the SHA and the raw `%B` message body. This makes a commit message
containing literal newlines — or even one that happened to contain the record separator
itself, if a commit author somehow typed it — unambiguous to split back into records, which a
newline- or blank-line-based delimiter could not guarantee. Parsing then splits each raw
message on its *first* blank line into `summary`/`body`, mirroring how `gix`'s own
commit-message parsing splits title from body on the native path, so both backends hand
callers byte-identical shapes. `--` before pathspecs and before `name`/`target_sha` in every
tag-writing command marks the end of option parsing, so a value that happens to start with `-`
(defended against upstream by `is_valid_git_ref_name`, but defended here too) is never
misread as a flag.

### V.6 `GitAccess` — backend selection (`access.rs`)

```rust
pub struct GitAccess<'r> { /* native: Option<GitRepository>, shell: ShellGit<'r> */ }

impl<'r> GitAccess<'r> {
    pub fn discover(root: impl AsRef<Path>, runner: &'r dyn CommandRunner) -> Self;
}
```

The type every caller outside this crate actually constructs (§9.4, §CL, §G.9). `discover`
never fails: it attempts native `gix` discovery and keeps the `Option<GitRepository>` result
either way, while unconditionally preparing a `ShellGit` against the same root as the
fallback (or sole) backend. A discovery failure — not a repo, or `wasm32` where `gix` is
excluded from the dependency set entirely — just means every operation on this `GitAccess`
runs through the shell.

**Fallback policy differs by operation category, deliberately:**

- **Reads** (`head_sha`, `list_tags`, `resolve_commit`, `commits_since`): fall back to the
  shell backend whenever native `gix` errors for *any* reason — failed discovery as well as a
  discovered repo's own operation failing. Retrying a read through the shell can only help: at
  worst it fails too and the error propagates from there instead.
- **Writes** (`create_tag`, `create_floating_major`): fall back to the shell *only* when
  native `gix` was never available to begin with (discovery failed). If a repo *was*
  discovered, its result — success or failure — is authoritative and returned as-is,
  never retried through the shell. Retrying a failed mutation through a second, different
  code path risks masking a genuine failure (e.g. "tag already exists") or double-applying a
  mutation the first attempt partially completed — a risk read-only retries don't carry.

`GitAccess` implements `GitDataSource` by trying `self.native`'s corresponding method first
(reads: `if let Ok(..) = ...`, falling through on any `Err`; writes: an unconditional early
`return` when `self.native` is `Some`, regardless of whether the call itself succeeds) and
falling back to `self.shell` only in the cases the policy above allows.

### V.7 `CommitWalker` integration — bridging to Layer 1 (`lib.rs`)

```rust
impl From<VcsError> for CommitWalkError { /* narrows to the Layer 1 vocabulary, below */ }
```

`callisto_model::CommitWalker` (§M.10) is a Layer 1 trait — it must not know `VcsError` exists,
since `callisto-model` depends on no `callisto-*` crate (§M.5). This crate bridges the gap:
`CommitWalkError::Command` and `CommitWalkError::RefNotFound` survive the narrowing as
themselves (the two distinctions Layer 1 callers branch on); every other `VcsError` variant —
`RepoNotFound`, `Git`, `InvalidGlob` — is gix- or repository-specific with no Layer 1
equivalent, so it collapses into `CommitWalkError::Backend { message }` carrying the original
`Display` rendering, losing nothing a user would see. `GitAccess`, `GitRepository`, and
`ShellGit` each get a `CommitWalker` impl whose body is identical (delegate `commits_since`,
map the error through the `From` above) — written via a macro rather than a blanket `impl<T:
GitDataSource> CommitWalker for T`, since `CommitWalker` is foreign to this crate and a
blanket impl over an uncovered type parameter is forbidden by Rust's orphan rules.

### V.8 Fixture obligations

Per §12.6's "broader than JSON shape alone" (this crate has no JSON output of its own — its
data feeds `callisto-graph`'s tag/commit logic, not stdout directly):

1. **Backend-parity corpus.** Every `GitDataSource` operation exercised against a real
   temporary repository (built with the real `git` binary, not mocked) through both
   `GitRepository` directly and `ShellGit` against a `CommandRunner` shelling that same real
   `git`, asserting identical results — this is what makes §V.3's "byte-identical regardless
   of backend" claim a tested property, not an aspiration.
2. **`GitAccess` selection corpus.** A poisoned `CommandRunner` (panics/errors on any
   invocation) proves a real-repo read never touches the shell; a non-repo root with a
   call-counting `CommandRunner` proves exactly one shell call serves the read fallback; a
   real repo with a failing write (`create_tag` on an already-existing name) proves the
   failure propagates without a rescue attempt through the poisoned shell.
3. **`commits_since` regression corpus.** The pre-tag-branch-commit scenario (§V.4) and the
   ref-not-found-must-error scenario (§V.4, §V.5), each proven independently through both
   backends.
4. **Glob-parity corpus.** The same malformed glob pattern against both backends, asserting
   `Err(VcsError::InvalidGlob)` from each — not "some" error, the specific variant, since a
   caller pattern-matches on it.
5. **`wasm32-wasip1` build check.** This crate must compile for that target (native `gix`
   `cfg`'d out, `GitRepository::discover` always `Err`) — no runtime test suite, since
   `callisto-moon` never constructs `GitRepository`/`GitAccess` directly (§V.0); a build
   failure here would still indicate a real problem (an accidental non-`cfg`-gated `gix` call).

### V.9 Index of `[SPEC DECISION]` flags

None. Every shape and policy in this section — the four `VcsError` codes, the read/write
fallback-policy split, the `CommitWalker` narrowing rule — is either pinned directly by
`00-design.md` §9.4/§13 or is existing, shipped behavior with no open reading of the design
doc left to resolve; this crate's section was written directly from source (§1's "traced back
to source" standard) rather than from a design-doc gap requiring a documented choice.

### 13.6 Native VCS Engine Architecture (`callisto-vcs` & `gix`)

**Purpose.** In-process Git operations powered by `gix` (gitoxide), eliminating subprocess
fork/exec overhead for repository discovery, ref matching, commit history revwalks, tag
filtering, and HEAD SHA retrieval where available, with a `CommandRunner`-shelled fallback
everywhere else. Full type signatures, the read/write fallback-policy split, and fixture
obligations live in **§12 (`callisto-vcs`)** — this subsection states the two MUST-level
requirements only; it is not a second, independent sketch of the crate's shapes.

   (`resolve_commit`), tag enumeration (`list_tags`), commit history revwalks
   (`commits_since_with_pathspec`), and HEAD SHA retrieval (`head_sha`) MUST be encapsulated
   within `callisto-vcs` using pure-Rust `gix` (§V.4) — never called directly by
   `callisto-graph` or `callisto-conventional`.

   read/write fallback-policy split (§V.6) that makes "seamlessly falls back to `CommandRunner`
   subprocess calls when `gix` is unavailable" true without each call site re-implementing the
   policy itself.

input.subject: Fix stale CommandRunner→CommitWalker doc drift in docs/01-spec.md §C.5/§C.7/§C.8 and M.13.3
input.description:
Discovered during task #25/#26's review pass (independent review agent + follow-up verification): docs/01-spec.md's §C.5 (`fetch_commits`), §C.7 (`infer_severity`), and §C.8 (`ConventionalError`) still show a pre-CommitWalker-refactor signature that no longer matches real source.

Real source (verified 2026-08-14):
- `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`: `fetch_commits(walker: &dyn CommitWalker, ...)`, not `runner: &dyn CommandRunner, cwd: &Path, ...` as §C.5 currently shows.
- `crates/callisto-conventional/src/infer.rs`: `infer_severity(walker: &dyn CommitWalker, ...)`, not `runner: &dyn CommandRunner, cwd: &Path, ...` as §C.7 currently shows.

Serializes updated documents using a custom formatter matching the fingerprinted indentation style and line endings (`LF` vs `CRLF`). 179 180 ### Atomic Disk Persistence (`atomic_write`) 181 182 To guarantee crash-safety during file writes: 183 184 ```rust 185 pub fn atomic_write(path: &Path, content: &str, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> io::Result<()> { 186 let parent_dir = path.parent().ok_or(...)?; 187 let mut temp_file = NamedTempFile::new_in(parent_dir)?; 188 temp_file.write_all(content.as_bytes())?; 189 temp_file.as_file().sync_all()?; 190 temp_file.persist(path)?; 191 // fsync parent and grandparent directories for durability after rename. 192 sync_dir(parent_dir)?; 193 if let Some(grandparent) = parent_dir.parent() { sync_dir(grandparent)?; } 194 Ok(()) 195 } 196 ``` 197 198 `ApplyPermit` is a capability token that must be obtained before any mutating operation (see §7). By creating `NamedTempFile` in the same directory as the target file, the final `fs::rename` is an atomic OS kernel operation on POSIX and Windows filesystems. Parent and grandparent directory fsyncs ensure the rename is durable on power-loss. 199 200 --- 201 202 ## 6. Dependency DAG Engine & Algorithmic Complexities 203 204 Workspace package relationships form a directed graph `G = (V, E)` where vertices $V$ represent `PackageId` nodes and edges $E$ represent dependency declarations. 205 206 ### Topological Sorting & Cycle Diagnostics 207 208 1. **Graph Construction**: `callisto-graph` builds a `petgraph::graph::DiGraph`. 209 2. **Cycle Detection (Tarjan's SCC Algorithm)**: 210 - Before calculating version bumps, `callisto-graph` executes Tarjan's Strongly Connected Components algorithm ($O(|V| + |E|)$ time, $O(|V|)$ space). 211 - If circular dependencies exist (e.g. $A \to B \to C \to A$), Callisto isolates the exact cycle path and formats a colorized `miette` diagnostic card: 212 213 ```text 214 Error: Circular dependency cycle detected in workspace graph 215 callisto-graph → callisto-manifests → callisto-graph 216 Tip: Refactor shared types into a common Layer 1 crate or mark peer dependencies. 217 ``` 218 219 3. **Topological Order Execution**: 220 - Executes Kahn's algorithm ($O(|V| + |E|)$) to establish linear build and publish ordering. 221 222 ### Bump Cascade Engine 223 224 When a package $P_A$ is bumped from version $V_{old}$ to $V_{new}$ with severity $S$: 225 226 ```mermaid 227 %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'lineColor': '#64748b', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#f8fafc', 'fontFamily': 'ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif'}}}%% 228 flowchart TD 229 Start(["Input: Package P_A
with Severity S"]) 230 Step1["Apply severity S to P_A
Calculate V_new"] 231 Step2{"Inspect Reverse
Dependencies of P_A"} 232 Step3["Calculate required bump for P_B
Re-enqueue (P_B, derived severity)"] 233 Step4["Update dependency range
in P_B manifest — no version bump"] 234 235 Start --> Step1 236 Step1 --> Step2 237 Step2 -- "Runtime Edge" --> Step3 238 Step2 -- "Dev / Peer Edge" --> Step4 239 Step3 -- "re-enqueue" --> Step2 240 241 style Start fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a 242 style Step1 fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#4338ca,color:#312e81 243 style Step2 fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#4c1d95 244 style Step3 fill:#d1fae5,stroke:#059669,color:#064e3b 245 style Step4 fill:#fed7aa,stroke:#ea580c,color:#7c2d12 246 ``` 247 248 ### Version Groups (Fixed & Linked) 249 250 `callisto.toml` supports version group rules: 251 - **`[[fixed-group]]`**: All packages in the group are forced to bump in lock-step to the maximum version calculated across any member in the group. 252 - **`[[linked-group]]`**: Packages in the group share severity bumps, but maintain independent base version offsets. 253 254 --- 255 256 ## 7. In-Process VCS Engine (`callisto-vcs`) 257 258 `callisto-vcs` provides Git operations through a dual-backend design: a native `gix` (gitoxide) backend for non-WASM targets, and a `ShellGit` backend that shells out to the real `git` binary for portability and WASM fallback. 259 260 ### Key VCS Capabilities 261 262 - **Repository Discovery**: Walks parent directories from the current working directory to locate `.git` (native backend only; shell backend uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`). 263 - **Commit Walks**: Retrieves commit history to evaluate conventional commits since a given Git ref or release tag. 264 - **Tag Listing**: Matches tags against glob patterns (`v*`, `@scope/*`) using `globset` (both backends apply identical `globset` matching semantics). 265 266 ### Dual-Backend Architecture (`GitAccess`) 267 268 `callisto-vcs` exposes a unified `GitDataSource` trait. The `GitAccess` selector implements it with a deliberate fallback policy: 269 270 - **Read operations** (`list_tags`, `resolve_commit`, `commits_since`): attempt the native `gix` backend first; fall back to `ShellGit` on any error, including failed repo discovery. 271 - **Write operations** (`create_tag`, `create_floating_major`): fall back to `ShellGit` only when native `gix` was unavailable from the start. A discovered repo's result is authoritative — a second backend retry could mask partial mutations. 272 273 ```rust 274 pub struct GitAccess<'r> { 275 native: Option, // None on wasm32 or outside a repo 276 shell: ShellGit<'r>, // always available via CommandRunner 277 } 278 ``` 279 280 ### WASM Target Constraints 281 282 `gix` depends on POSIX signal handlers (`gix-tempfile` -> `signal-hook-registry`), which are unsupported on `wasm32-wasip1`. `GitRepository::discover` always returns `Err` on that target (via a compile-time feature gate), so `GitAccess` automatically routes all operations through `ShellGit`, which calls `git` via the Extism host bridge. 283 284 Note: a 2026 probe confirmed that `gix` object reads fail with `ENOSYS` on WASM even with the signal-hook dependency removed. The shell-git fallback is therefore the production code path for the Moon WASM plugin. 285 286 --- 287 288 ## 8. Extension Architecture & Trait Seams 289 290 Callisto decouples core algorithms from platform-specific I/O using four core trait seams: 291 292 ```rust 293 // 1. Locate workspace project roots 294 pub trait ProjectLocator { 295 fn projects(&self) -> Result, LocateError>; 296 } 297 298 // 2. Command execution abstraction 299 pub trait CommandRunner: Send + Sync { 300 fn run(&self, program: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path) -> Result; 301 302 // Default: delegates to run(). CliCommandRunner overrides with real 303 // spawn + poll + kill so that hung publish commands do not block forever. 304 fn run_with_timeout(&self, program: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path, timeout: Duration) 305 -> Result; 306 } 307 308 // 4. Per-ecosystem manifest reader/writer 309 pub trait Manifest { 310 fn path(&self) -> &Path; 311 fn ecosystem(&self) -> Ecosystem; 312 fn role(&self) -> ManifestRole; 313 fn package_name(&self) -> Result; 314 fn current_version(&self) -> Result; 315 fn write_version(&mut self, new_version: &Version, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>; 316 fn iter_dependencies(&self) -> Box + '_>; 317 fn update_dependency_spec(&mut self, name: &str, new_spec: DepSpec, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>; 318 fn update_optional_dependencies(&mut self, name: &str, new_spec: DepSpec, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<(), ManifestError>; 319 // publish_targets() and persist() are also required; omitted for brevity. 320 } 321 322 // 5. DependencyResolver supplies graph nodes and edges 323 pub trait DependencyResolver { 324 fn packages(&self) -> impl Iterator; 325 fn dependencies_of(&self, id: &PackageId) -> impl Iterator; 326 fn dependents_of(&self, id: &PackageId) -> impl Iterator; 327 // diagnostics() has a default impl returning an empty slice. 328 } 329 ``` 330 331 ### Moon WASM Plugin Binding (`callisto-moon`) 332 333 `callisto-moon` compiles Callisto into a `wasm32-wasip1` plugin using `extism-pdk`. Moon loads `callisto-moon.wasm` inside Extism, passing host environment queries through Extism FFI exports (`#[plugin_fn]`). 334 335 --- 336 337 ## 9. workflow_dispatch 351 Verify->>Verify: format · lint · test · WASM check · cargo-deny audit 352 alt CI Fails 353 Verify-->>Runner: Exit 1 — Job 2 cancelled 354 else CI Passes 355 Verify->>Action: PR Pre-Flight Verification & Local Git Hooks 393 394 ### PR Pre-Flight Verification (`callisto-validate`) 395 396 Every Pull Request runs the standalone [`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) action: 397 1. **Package Discovery Guard**: Verifies all workspace crates and packages are accounted for in `callisto.toml`. 398 2. **Schema & Config Health**: Validates `callisto.toml` fields and types. 399 3. **Changeset Syntax Integrity**: Verifies `.changeset/*.md` frontmatter and package IDs. 400 4. **Pre-Flight Release Simulation**: Simulates `callisto plan-publish` topological DAG sorting to ensure zero cyclic dependencies before PR merge. 401 402 ### Ultra-Fast Local Git Hooks (`pre-commit` & `pre-push`) 403 404 Callisto standardizes local developer hook workflows in [`justfile`](justfile): 405 - `just pre-commit` (~100ms): Fast formatting check before local commits. 406 - `just pre-push` (~1.5s): Formatting check and Clippy lints before remote pushes. 407 - `just hooks`: Installs native `.git/hooks/pre-commit` and `.git/hooks/pre-push` shell scripts in one command. 408 409 --- 410 411 ## 11. input.description: Verify secret-redaction fixes across 4 crates
input.prompt:
You are reviewing uncommitted changes to the Callisto Rust workspace at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto. Run `git diff` (or per-file `git diff -- <path>`) to see the exact changes across these 5 files:
- crates/callisto-model/src/registry.rs
- crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs
- crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/validate.rs
- crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs
- crates/callisto-conventional/src/pre_cursor.rs

Do not trust any summary from me — read the actual diff and the actual current source yourself.

## What changed and why

This closes a real security gap: several places in the codebase construct an error type (`GraphError`, `VcsError`, `ConventionalError`) directly from a failed `git` subprocess's raw stderr, with no redaction. If `git` ever echoes an authenticated remote URL in its own error output (the realistic case: a GitHub Actions checkout using `REDACTED` as its remote, then some `git` operation failing and printing that URL back), the token could flow unredacted into a `--format json` report, a miette diagnostic card, or a CI log. This mirrors an already-shipped fix (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs`'s `redact_stderr` helper, wrapping `callisto_model::redact_known_secrets`/`known_credential_env_values`) that was applied only to npm/cargo/twine registry-publish stderr, not `git` subprocess stderr.

Changes:
1. `callisto-model/src/registry.rs`: `known_credential_env_values` now also matches `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` env var names (previously only `NPM_TOKEN`/`TWINE_PASSWORD`/`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`/`CARGO_REGISTRIES_*_TOKEN`).
2. `callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`: a new `pub(crate) fn redact_git_stderr` wraps `redact_known_secrets(text, &known_credential_env_values(std::env::vars()))`; the two `git add`/`git rm --cached` staging-failure sites (building `GraphError::Command(CommandError::Failed { stderr, .. })`) now call it instead of embedding `output.stderr` raw.
3. `callisto-graph/src/commands/validate.rs`: the two `git diff --cached`/`git diff <range>` failure sites (building `GraphError::Command(CommandError::Io { message, .. })`) now call `crate::apply::redact_git_stderr` (reusing #2's helper across the crate) instead of embedding `out.stderr` raw.
4. `callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs`: a new private `fn redact_git_stderr` (this crate's own copy, since it's a separate crate from callisto-graph); all four `VcsError::Git(format!(...))` sites (`head_sha`, `commits_since`, `create_tag`, `create_floating_major`) now redact `output.stderr` before embedding it.
5. `callisto-conventional/src/pre_cursor.rs`: a new private `fn redact_git_stderr` (this crate's own copy); both `ConventionalError::MalformedPreCursorRef`/`PreCursorAdvanceFailed` construction sites now redact `output.stderr` before embedding it.

Each file's fix is accompanied by a real, previously-red-now-green test using a fake `CommandRunner` whose canned response contains a GitHub-Actions-shaped authenticated URL (`REDACTED`) in stderr, asserting the resulting error's rendered text does not contain `ghs_leaked_secret` and does contain `[REDACTED]`.

A separate site, `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`, was investigated and deliberately NOT touched — it only constructs `CommandOutput { stderr: ... }` (a raw data-relay struct returned from `CommandRunner::run`), never an error/diagnostic type. Redaction happens downstream wherever a caller turns that `CommandOutput` into a displayed/serialized error — which is exactly what files #2-5 above do. Verify this reasoning holds: confirm `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs` truly never constructs an error containing raw stderr (only `CommandOutput`), and that nothing downstream of `MoonCommandRunner::run` bypasses the fixed call sites.

## Your job

1. **Verify every fix is real and correctly wired.** For each of the 4 source files with a new `redact_git_stderr` (or the `known_credential_env_values` extension), confirm the call site actually invokes it (not just defines it unused), and that no OTHER raw-stderr-into-error site in the same file was missed. Grep each file for `stderr` and `.stderr` to check for any sibling site that still embeds raw stderr un-redacted.
2. **Verify the tests are real, not tautological.** For each new test, confirm it actually exercises the real code path (not a test that would pass regardless of whether the fix exists) — check that the fake runner's response really reaches the error-construction line being tested, and that the assertion checks the rendered/serialized error text (not some internal field that bypasses `Display`).
3. **Check for scope gaps.** Search the whole workspace (not just these 5 files) for any OTHER place that constructs `GraphError`/`VcsError`/`ConventionalError`/`CliError` (or embeds subprocess stderr into a `Diagnostic`/report field) directly from a `git` subprocess's `output.stderr` without going through one of these new helpers — a sibling gap the task should have caught but didn't. Pay particular attention to `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/changed.rs`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs`, and anywhere else in `callisto-graph`/`callisto-cli` that shells out to `git` directly (not through `GitAccess`/`GitDataSource`, which already redacts via #4).
4. **Check the moon/runner.rs reasoning.** Confirm the claim above — that `runner.rs` is correctly out of scope — actually holds, by reading the file and tracing what calls `MoonCommandRunner::run` and what those callers do with a non-success `CommandOutput`.
5. **Check for regressions.** Confirm `redact_known_secrets`'s existing behavior (URL-userinfo stripping, empty-secret guard) is unaffected — this task only added new call sites and one new env-var-name pair, no logic change to the redaction primitives themselves.

Report every issue found as a concrete finding: file, line, what's wrong, and what the correct fix would be. If you find a real sibling gap (a 6th+ site that should have been fixed but wasn't), report it clearly with the exact file:line and the raw-stderr code path, since that's the most likely real defect. Do not report style preferences. If everything checks out, say so explicitly and state what you checked. Keep the report under 700 words unless multiple real gaps need detail.

## Context

This is a follow-up fix in a larger task that already redacted subprocess-stderr-into-error leaks at 4 other sites across 3 crates (callisto-graph's apply.rs/commands/validate.rs, callisto-vcs's shell.rs, callisto-conventional's pre_cursor.rs) — each using the same pattern: a local `redact_git_stderr(text) -> String` wrapping `callisto_model::redact_known_secrets(text, &callisto_model::known_credential_env_values(std::env::vars()))`, applied before embedding raw `git` subprocess stderr into a displayed/serialized error type. An independent review of those 4 fixes found a 5th, previously-missed site: `pre.rs`'s `pre enter` handler ran `git add .changeset/pre.json` and embedded `output.stderr` raw into `CliError::Other` on failure — the same leak class, just in a different crate (callisto-cli).

The fix: extracted the git-add-and-check logic out of the inline `handle()` body into a new private function `fn stage_pre_json(runner: &dyn CommandRunner, root: &Path) -> Result<(), CliError>`, added a local `redact_git_stderr` helper (mirroring the other 4 crates' copies), wired `redact_git_stderr(&output.stderr)` into the error-construction site inside `stage_pre_json`, and added a new `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (this file previously had none) with one test using a fake `CommandRunner` returning a GitHub-Actions-shaped credential-bearing stderr, asserting the resulting `CliError`'s rendered text doesn't contain the raw secret and does contain `[REDACTED]`. `handle()`'s call site was changed from ~9 lines of inline git-add-and-check logic to a single `stage_pre_json(&runner, &ws.root)?;` call.

The fix author manually verified the test is non-tautological via a temporary mutation (reverting `redact_git_stderr(&output.stderr)` to `output.stderr.clone()`, confirming the test fails, then restoring the fix) — you don't need to repeat that, but you may spot-check it if you want extra confidence.

## Your job

1. **Verify the extraction preserved behavior exactly.** Compare the old inline logic (visible as removed lines in the diff) against the new `stage_pre_json` function — same git command (`git add .changeset/pre.json`... wait, verify it's actually `git add` with the `PRE_JSON_REL` constant, not a hardcoded string that could have drifted), same error message format for both the run-failure case (`CliError::Other(format!("git add failed: {e}"))`) and the non-success-exit case, same behavior when `output.success()` is true (returns `Ok(())`) — nothing was silently changed beyond adding redaction.
2. **Verify `handle()`'s call site is correct.** Confirm `stage_pre_json(&runner, &ws.root)?` is called with the right arguments, in the right place (after the atomic write, same as before), and that the `?` propagates the error the same way the old inline `return Err(...)` did.
3. **Verify the test is real.** Confirm the fake `CommandRunner`'s `run` method signature actually matches the real `callisto_model::CommandRunner` trait (check `crates/callisto-model/src/exec.rs`), confirm `stage_pre_json` is actually `pub(crate)` or otherwise reachable from the `tests` submodule (check the `use super::stage_pre_json;` import resolves), and confirm the assertion checks `format!("{err}")` — i.e., the actual `Display` output a JSON/text renderer would show a user, not some internal field.
4. **Check for any other now-broken caller.** Grep the whole crate for any other place that called the old inline pattern or referenced the removed code, to make sure nothing else needed updating.

input.description: Verify IdentityIndex.platform wiring fix
input.prompt:
You are reviewing an uncommitted change to the Callisto Rust workspace at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto, spanning `crates/callisto-graph/src/identity.rs`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`, and `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs`. Run `git diff -- crates/callisto-graph/src/identity.rs crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs` to see the exact changes. Do not trust any summary from me — read the diff and current source yourself, and be skeptical: this fix required unusually deep architectural investigation before being written, which is exactly the kind of situation where a subtle mistake is easy to miss.

## Background — what was broken and why

`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`'s workspace-discovery loop already detected napi platform npm packages (via `detect_npm_role`, which reads a `package.json`'s `os`/`cpu` fields) and pushed a `ManifestDecl` with `ManifestRole::Platform` into a package's manifest list (used for publish routing). But it never inserted anything into `IdentityIndex.platform` — a `BTreeMap` that `crate::config::groups::GroupTable::resolve` consults as a fallback when a `[[fixed-group]]`/`[[linked-group]]` config's `members` list names something that doesn't resolve to a real registered `Package` (i.e. a platform package, which per the spec's own SPEC DECISION at docs/01-spec.md:769 is *never* an independently-registered `Package` — it's an extra manifest belonging to some other, owning `Package`). Without this index populated, any `callisto.toml` naming a platform package's own npm name in a group's `members` list would fail hard with `GraphError::MissingGroupMember`, and `napi_drift` (in `crates/callisto-graph/src/napi.rs`) — which computes `member_triples` by reading `role_to_triple` off each group's `GroupMember::PlatformManifest` members — would never receive any real platform members to check against declared `napi.targets`.

## The fix (three coordinated changes)

1. **`identity.rs`**: `IdentityIndex.platform`'s value type changed from `(PackageId, PathBuf)` to `(PackageId, PathBuf, ManifestRole)` — the role is now carried in the index itself (computed once in walk.rs, where `detect_npm_role` already produced it) rather than needing a second/third disk read downstream. The `platforms_of` method's tuple-destructuring was updated to match (it has zero current callers anywhere in the workspace — confirm this).

2. **`walk.rs`**: in the per-manifest loop that builds `IdentityIndex`, the loop variable was renamed from `_id` (discarded) to `id` (now used). When `detect_npm_role` classifies a manifest as `ManifestRole::Platform`, the fix now inserts `index.platform.insert(id.name().to_string(), (primary_id.clone(), manifest_rel, role))`. The key insight the fix author reasoned through: `id` is *this specific manifest's own* npm-ecosystem identity (resolved from its own `package.json` `name` field by the project locator) — which is **distinct from `primary_id`** whenever a higher-priority ecosystem (Cargo) shares the same directory as this npm manifest (a "Case D" dual-ecosystem project, where `primary_id` is chosen as the Cargo identity per `ecosystem_primary_priority`, but the npm manifest sharing that directory has its own separate name). Config authors write the platform package's *own* npm name into `[[fixed-group]] members`, so that must be the index key — `primary_id` is recorded as the *owner* in the tuple's value, not the key.

3. **`config/groups.rs`**: both `GroupTable::resolve` call sites (`raw.fixed` and `raw.linked` loops) that previously hardcoded `role: ManifestRole::Platform { platform: "unknown".to_string(), arch: "unknown".to_string(), abi: None }` (which `napi.rs::role_to_triple` can never map to a real triple — verify this claim yourself against `role_to_triple`'s match table) now destructure the real `role` from `index.platform.get(name)` and use it directly.

A new end-to-end test was added in `walk.rs`'s test module: `real_platform_manifest_resolves_via_fixed_group_and_feeds_napi_drift`. It builds a real temp directory with a `Cargo.toml` (crate `my-crate`) and a `package.json` in the *same* directory named `@myorg/my-crate-linux-x64-gnu` with `os:["linux"], cpu:["x64"]` (a genuine Case D layout — verify `x64`/`linux` with no ABI field really does map to `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` via `detect_npm_role`'s Linux-ABI-from-name-suffix inference, given the package name ends in `-linux-x64-gnu`), a `callisto.toml` with a `[[fixed-group]]` naming both `"my-crate"` and `"@myorg/my-crate-linux-x64-gnu"` as members, calls `Workspace::load`, and asserts: group resolution succeeds (not `Err(MissingGroupMember)`), the resolved `GroupMember::PlatformManifest`'s `role` maps via `role_to_triple` to `Some("x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")` (not the old "unknown" stub), and feeding the group into `napi_drift` with that declared triple produces zero drift diagnostics.

The fix author verified this test fails for the right reason (`Err(MissingGroupMember)`) when the `index.platform.insert(...)` line is temporarily disabled, then restored the fix and confirmed the test passes again (via a manual before/after diff comparison) — you don't need to repeat that, but you're welcome to if you want independent confirmation.

## Your job

1. **Verify the Case D key-selection reasoning is actually correct**, not just plausible-sounding. Trace through `by_path`'s construction (`walk.rs`, the loop building `by_path: BTreeMap<PathBuf, Vec<(Ecosystem, PackageId)>>`) and confirm that when a directory has both a `Cargo.toml` and a differently-named `package.json`, the `list` for that path really does contain two distinct `(Ecosystem, PackageId)` entries with different `.name()` values, and that `primary_id = list[0].1.clone()` really does pick the Cargo one (verify `ecosystem_primary_priority`'s ordering). If this reasoning has a hole, it's the most likely place for a real bug.
2. **Verify the type change's blast radius was fully handled.** Grep the whole workspace (not just the 3 changed files) for every place that pattern-matches or destructures `IdentityIndex.platform`'s value tuple, to confirm nothing else needed updating and nothing was missed (the build already succeeds per the author, but confirm independently — a stale cached build could mask this).
3. **Verify `role_to_triple`'s "unknown" stub claim.** Confirm directly against `napi.rs`'s `role_to_triple` match table that `ManifestRole::Platform { platform: "unknown", arch: "unknown", abi: None }` really does fall through to `_ => return None` — i.e. that the pre-fix hardcoded stub really was useless, not just suboptimal.
4. **Verify the test itself is sound**, not just that it passes. In particular: does `Workspace::load` really invoke `GroupTable::resolve` internally (trace the actual call chain), or could the test be accidentally passing/failing for an unrelated reason? Does `detect_npm_role`'s Linux-ABI-inference-from-package-name-suffix logic really produce `abi: Some("gnu")` for a package literally named `...-linux-x64-gnu` (check the suffix-matching function directly, don't assume)? Is there any hidden dependency on test-run ordering, shared global state, or filesystem side effects between this test and others in the same file (e.g. `PERSIST_CALL_COUNT`-style global counters were flagged elsewhere in this codebase as a real hazard for tests in the same binary — check whether anything comparable is at risk here)?
5. **Check for a sibling gap**: is there any OTHER place in the codebase that constructs a `GroupMember::PlatformManifest` (or otherwise needs to resolve a platform package's identity/role) that still uses the old, now-removed hardcoded stub pattern, or that bypasses `index.platform` entirely and could regress once real data flows through it? Search specifically for other `ManifestRole::Platform { platform: "unknown"` or similar placeholder constructions anywhere in `crates/callisto-graph/src/`.
6. **Run the real checks yourself**: `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib`, `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Don't trust that they were clean when someone else ran them — confirm it fresh.

Report every issue found as a concrete finding: file, line, what's wrong, and what the correct fix would be. If the Case D reasoning or the test turns out to be unsound, that's the most important thing to flag clearly and in detail. If everything checks out, say so explicitly and summarize what you verified for each of the 6 items. Keep the report under 700 words unless multiple real issues need detail.

input.subject: Fix index.native's Case D key mismatch for platform package dependency edges
input.description:
Discovered during task #31's review (independent review agent, not a defect in that task's diff — flagged explicitly as out-of-scope/pre-existing).

In `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`'s identity-building loop (~line 121-123), `index.native.insert((*eco, primary_id.name().to_string()), primary_id.clone())` keys the native (ecosystem, name) -> PackageId index on `primary_id.name()` for every ecosystem entry in `list`, rather than that specific entry's own `id.name()`.

In a Case D directory (a Cargo.toml and a differently-named package.json sharing one directory — the same scenario task #31 fixed for `index.platform`), this means the npm-ecosystem manifest's own name (e.g. a platform package like `@myorg/my-crate-linux-x64-gnu`) never gets a `native` index entry under its own name — only under the Cargo-derived `primary_id`'s name. If some OTHER npm manifest declares a dependency (e.g. `optionalDependencies`) on that platform package by its literal own npm name, `index.native.get((Ecosystem::Npm, "@myorg/my-crate-linux-x64-gnu"))` would return `None` and the dependency edge would silently fail to resolve, with no diagnostic.

Likely fix (needs verification, not yet investigated in depth): use `id.name()` (the per-ecosystem entry's own resolved identity, same variable task #31 already renamed from `_id` to `id` for the analogous `index.platform` fix) instead of `primary_id.name()` when inserting into `index.native`, mirroring task #31's exact reasoning. Needs its own red test proving a real optionalDependencies edge onto a Case D platform package currently fails to resolve, then the fix, then verification it resolves correctly — full TDD rigor per this session's standing process.
